# OccurrenceCleaner

*quality flags for occurrence records, at any scale*

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner)
[![License:
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

OccurrenceCleaner is an extension of
[CoordinateCleaner](https://ropensci.github.io/CoordinateCleaner/)
(Zizka et al. 2019) tailored to large-scale occurrence data. It flags
common problems in species occurrence records: coordinates at country
centroids, capitals or biodiversity institutions; zero or equal
coordinates; records at sea, in the wrong country or outside the species
range; duplicates; records far from the rest of their species; and
datasets whose coordinates were converted from degrees and minutes or
published on a grid.

It also reads three fields GBIF fills for each record: the quality
warnings GBIF attaches during processing, the basis of record and the
establishment means.

Records are flagged and kept, and users choose afterwards which flags to
filter on.

The input is any table of records with Darwin Core coordinate and
species columns: a GBIF download (for example from rgbif), a whole GBIF
snapshot, or another aggregator’s export. Taxonomic name cleaning is not
part of the package.

Records usually come from
[rgbif](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rgbif) (GBIF) or
[paleobioDB](https://cran.r-project.org/package=paleobioDB) (the
Paleobiology Database), with names matched beforehand, for example with
[taxize](https://cran.r-project.org/package=taxize). The kept records go
on to species distribution models such as
[dismo](https://cran.r-project.org/package=dismo) or
[sdm](https://cran.r-project.org/package=sdm), or, for fossils, to
PyRate through
[`export_pyrate()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/export_pyrate.md).

The tests are reimplemented with CoordinateCleaner’s definitions,
default buffers and settings, and CoordinateCleaner itself is needed
only to compare: the test suite runs it on sampled records and checks
that both packages return the same flags; the few deliberate differences
are listed in [Coming from
CoordinateCleaner](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/articles/coordinatecleaner.html).

Data frames containing a few million records are flagged in seconds
([timings](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/articles/coordinatecleaner.html#speed)),
and GBIF snapshots containing billions of records are processed by
reading Parquet files in chunks.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner")
```

Needs a C++ compiler (Rtools on Windows).

## Flag a data frame

``` r

library(OccurrenceCleaner)

x <- data.frame(species = c("Quercus robur", "Quercus robur", "Fagus sylvatica"),
                decimalLongitude = c(12.58, 0, 16.37),
                decimalLatitude = c(55.67, 0, 48.21))
flag_occurrences(x)
```

The result is `x` with one logical `flag_<test>` column per test and an
integer `flags` column that holds all of them, one bit per test. The
first record is within 1 km of the GBIF headquarters and 10 km of
Copenhagen, the second is a zero coordinate at sea, the third is in
Vienna, a capital.

## Several rules from one pass

A rule is a set of tests.
[`has_flag()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_mask.md)
marks the records a rule removes, and
[`tally_flags()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/tally_flags.md)
compares several rules on the same flags:

``` r

f <- flag_occurrences(x, tests = c("invalid", "zero", "equal", "capital", "centroid",
                                  "institution", "gbif_headquarters", "sea"))

strict <- c("zero", "equal", "capital", "centroid", "institution", "gbif_headquarters", "sea")
mild   <- c("zero", "equal", "gbif_headquarters")

has_flag(f$flags, strict)
tally_flags(f, by = "species", rules = list(strict = strict, mild = mild))
```

[`tally_flags()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/tally_flags.md)
gives, per group, the number of records each test flags and the number
each rule removes and keeps. Year and coordinate uncertainty stay raw
columns and are cut at tally time with `bins`.

## Outliers and dataset tests

The outlier and dataset tests judge a record against the rest of its
species or dataset, so they run in a pass over the whole input before
the record tests, streamed input included. Their options go in
`settings`, with CoordinateCleaner’s defaults:

``` r

flag_occurrences(occ, tests = c("invalid", "outlier", "dataset_ddmm", "dataset_rounded"),
                 settings = list(outlier = list(method = "mad")))
```

Fossil records from the Paleobiology Database add an age test and the
outlier tests of `clean_fossils()`, with the PBDB column names given
once:

``` r

flag_occurrences(pbdb, tests = c("invalid", "zero", "centroid", "institution", "age_equal",
                                 "age_range_outlier", "spatiotemporal_outlier"),
                 columns = occ_columns(lon = "lng", lat = "lat", species = "accepted_name"))
```

## A whole GBIF snapshot

The same verb streams an on-disk table through
[vectra](https://cran.r-project.org/package=vectra): a directory of
Parquet parts (a GBIF snapshot), a `.vtr` file, a delimited file or any
`vectra_node`. Each input file is one resumable unit, and the flags are
written as `.vtr` parts next to the columns you keep for grouping:

``` r

f <- flag_occurrences("gbif_snapshot/occurrence.parquet",
                      tests = c(default_tests(), "country_mismatch", "issue_rounded",
                                "basis_fossil"),
                      out = "flags",
                      keep = c("kingdom", "year", "coordinateuncertaintyinmeters"))

tally_flags(f, by = "kingdom",
            bins = list(year = c(1950, 1970, 1990, 2000),
                        coordinateuncertaintyinmeters = c(10, 100, 1000)),
            rules = list(cc = c("zero", "equal", "capital", "centroid", "institution",
                                "gbif_headquarters", "sea")))
```

Rerunning the same call after an interruption skips the input files
already finished.

## What’s in the box

- **[`flag_occurrences()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_occurrences.md)**:
  the one flagging verb. Data frame in, data frame out; path or
  `vectra_node` in, flag parts on disk out. `buffers` sets the proximity
  distances and `settings` the options of the outlier and dataset tests,
  both with CoordinateCleaner’s defaults.
- **[`tally_flags()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/tally_flags.md)**:
  per group, the number of records each test flags and each rule removes
  and keeps, with bins and named rules.
- **[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html)**,
  **[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html)**: the
  percentage of records each test and rule removes, and how much of it
  each test is the sole reason for; bars, a grid by group, or a map of
  kept and removed records.
- **[`has_flag()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_mask.md)**,
  **[`flag_mask()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_mask.md)**:
  which records a rule removes, read from the `flags` column.
- **[`flag_tests()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_tests.md)**:
  which bit of `flags` holds which test, with its definition, source and
  CoordinateCleaner equivalent; versioned.
- **[`default_tests()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/default_tests.md)**:
  the CoordinateCleaner-equivalent tests that need only coordinates and
  a species name.
- **[`occ_columns()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/occ_columns.md)**:
  which columns hold which field (coordinates, species, country code,
  fossil ages, dataset key, GBIF fields); Darwin Core defaults,
  case-insensitive.
- **[`reference_info()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/reference_info.md)**,
  **[`download_reference()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/download_reference.md)**:
  the pinned gazetteers (source, version, SHA-256) and the on-demand
  1:10m land layer.
- **[`reference_points()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/reference_points.md)**:
  the points a proximity test uses (capitals, centroids, institutions,
  GBIF headquarters, artificial hotspots), to inspect, filter or extend
  and pass back through `gazetteers`.
- **[`read_flagged()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/read_flagged.md)**,
  **[`flagged_table()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/read_flagged.md)**:
  open on-disk flag output as a vectra table.
- **[`export_pyrate()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/export_pyrate.md)**:
  write fossil records as PyRate input files.

## Tests

| test | definition | source |
|----|----|----|
| `invalid` | coordinate missing or out of range | `cc_val` |
| `zero` | zero longitude or latitude, or within 0.5 degrees of (0, 0) | `cc_zero` |
| `equal` | absolute longitude equals absolute latitude | `cc_equ` |
| `capital` | within 10 km of a capital | `cc_cap` |
| `centroid` | within 1 km of a country or province centroid | `cc_cen` |
| `institution` | within 100 m of a biodiversity institution | `cc_inst` |
| `gbif_headquarters` | within 1 km of the GBIF headquarters | `cc_gbif` |
| `sea` | outside the land polygons (Natural Earth, scale 110, 50 or 10) | `cc_sea` |
| `urban` | inside an urban area | `cc_urb` |
| `country_mismatch` | outside the country given by the record’s country code | `cc_coun` |
| `duplicate` | same coordinates and species as an earlier record | `cc_dupl` |
| `range` | outside every range polygon of its species (user-supplied ranges) | `cc_iucn` |
| `aohi` | within 10 km of an artificial hotspot (Park et al. 2023) | `cc_aohi` |
| `outlier` | far from the other records of its species | `cc_outl` |
| `dataset_ddmm` | in a dataset whose coordinates look converted from degrees and minutes | `cd_ddmm` |
| `dataset_rounded` | in a dataset whose coordinates lie on a regular grid | `cd_round` |
| `age_equal` | fossil minimum age equal to or greater than the maximum age | `cf_equal` |
| `age_outlier` | fossil age far from the ages of its taxon | `cf_age` |
| `spatiotemporal_outlier` | fossil far from its taxon in space and time | `cf_outl` |
| `age_range_outlier` | fossil age range unusually wide | `cf_range` |
| `issue_coordinate`, `issue_taxon`, `issue_date`, `issue_rounded` | GBIF quality warnings (`issue` field) on coordinates, taxon match, date, rounding | addition |
| `basis_fossil`, `basis_living` | basis of record | addition |
| `establishment_introduced`, `establishment_managed` | establishment means | addition |

Proximity tests are closed balls in WGS84 geodesic distance, found with
a kd-tree on the unit sphere and decided with the Vincenty inverse
formula. Polygon tests are planar point-in-polygon against pinned
Natural Earth layers through a grid index that resolves boundary cells
exactly.

The gazetteers are rebuilt from the original public sources (Natural
Earth, public domain; GBIF GRSciColl for institutions), each pinned to a
version and checksum. `reference = "CoordinateCleaner"` reads that
package’s own tables instead and gives its flags up to the documented
differences, which
[`?flag_occurrences`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_occurrences.md)
lists and the test suite enforces. The `gazetteers` argument replaces
the layer of single tests with the user’s own points or polygons,
recorded with the flags by size and checksum.

## Acknowledgements

The tests, their default buffers and the options of the outlier and
dataset tests come from CoordinateCleaner by Alexander Zizka and
co-authors (Zizka et al. 2019), an rOpenSci package. Its documented
definitions are what the equivalence tests check against, and the
gazetteers here are rebuilt from the public sources it draws on.

## License

MIT. CoordinateCleaner (GPL-3) is a suggested package used by the
equivalence tests and by `reference = "CoordinateCleaner"`; none of its
code or data is bundled.

## Rules and tallies

- [`tally_flags()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/tally_flags.md)
  : Tally flags into a loss table
- [`summary(`*`<occ_flags>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/summary.occ_flags.md)
  [`summary(`*`<occ_flagged>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/summary.occ_flags.md)
  [`summary(`*`<occ_tally>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/summary.occ_flags.md)
  : Share of records flagged, per test and rule
- [`plot(`*`<occ_summary>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/plot.occ_summary.md)
  [`plot(`*`<occ_tally>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/plot.occ_summary.md)
  [`plot(`*`<occ_flags>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/plot.occ_summary.md)
  [`plot(`*`<occ_flagged>`*`)`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/plot.occ_summary.md)
  : Plot flag percentages, or map flagged records

  : Bit mask and membership for sets of tests
- [`flag_tests()`](https://gillescolling.com/OccurrenceCleaner/reference/flag_tests.md)
  : The flag layout: one bit per test
